trigger: first boot of a server loading the embedded seed pack
classification_rationale: The seed spelled one product with two vendor values, so the pack load minted two product rows, and the seed loads once and is never replaced by a newer binary
summary: PostgreSQL, MySQL and LibreOffice were spelled with different vendors across rows (and 'The Document Foundation' reduces to 'the document'), giving one product two product_ids. Fixed: one vendor spelling per product (postgresql, oracle, libreoffice); the pack parser now rejects two rows sharing a norm_key with a different category or cpe_product, cpe_product '-' or '.', a NUL byte, and enforces byte, row and field caps; a seed test asserts one norm_key per (product, edition, cpe_product).

trigger: an installed-software report whose name, publisher and ecosystem are each 1024 incompressible bytes
classification_rationale: Ingest bounds each field but not their sum, so a triple can exceed the btree entry limit of title_triples' primary key and roll back the whole hourly catalogue refresh
summary: Probe on the private Postgres 18 reproduced 'index row size 3096 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704'. Fixed (adapted, no digest re-key): the title_triples INSERT keeps only triples whose combined octet_length is at most 2400, with the derivation in a comment; a [pg] test ingests a 3x1024 triple and asserts the refresh succeeds and the triple is absent; the manual states such titles are excluded. catalog_rollup_grain_key has the same class and is not changed here.

trigger: title_triples empty or never built (rollup stalled, fresh boot, no inventory)
classification_rationale: An empty feed produced a ratio of 0 with a successful tick, which reads as perfect coverage and documented '0 when no inventory'
summary: Fixed: the ratio gauge is not set while the title source is empty; both alert descriptions point at the catalogue-rollup alerts; the metrics manual, observability conventions, the describe() help text and the inventory manual are corrected, with the rollup-ceiling symptom stated.

trigger: a rejected curation-queue row whose title later resolves
classification_rationale: The pass's queue delete had no status filter while the header and migration comment say rejected rows persist
summary: Fixed: the delete is limited to status = 'open'; a [pg] test shows a rejected row survives its title resolving.

trigger: a fresh boot or the v9 upgrade, before the catalogue rollup has filled title_triples
classification_rationale: The first tick ran before the rollup filled the candidate table and the next was an hour away, contradicting the 'drains in minutes' wording
summary: Fixed (adapted): a pass that finds no candidate, an empty title_triples and non-empty installed_software reports source_pending; the tick carries the flag and the job re-arms after 60 s. The installed_software guard keeps a fleet with no inventory from polling. Header and manual wording corrected.

trigger: every pass's alias read
classification_rationale: The alias read filtered the leading primary-key column with a LIKE prefix, so it was a scan of product_aliases
summary: Fixed: the read takes the exact candidate sources (tier x the page's ecosystems plus the wildcard) as source = ANY(...); no new index.

trigger: a raw name that reduces to nothing (2019, (x64), Pro) or a normalized row whose product was deleted
classification_rationale: An empty normalised title fell through to unnormalized only by accident of the parser and auto-birth being off, and the gauge counted a product-less normalized row as normalized
summary: Fixed: an explicit guard in resolve_title with a test that has a positive control; the gauge query classifies a normalized row with a NULL product as pending, asserted in the gauge test.

trigger: a future writer or a stale schema_meta
classification_rationale: title_dimension had no CHECK on norm_status, method or category, the pack version accepted any month, and the registry constructor had no projection read
summary: Fixed (adapted on the version question): CHECK constraints on the three columns, month 01-12, a post-migration projection read of all five tables with a test that renames every column away, and the header states that a normaliser change requires a pack_version bump instead of a version column.

trigger: a future curation write setting pack_version = '' without the normalisation lock
classification_rationale: The invalidation contract required the sentinel write in the same transaction but did not require the normalisation lock, so a concurrent pass could overwrite the sentinel
summary: Fixed: the header, the ADR update and the software-estate routed-concern row state that the write MUST first take the blocking pg_advisory_xact_lock on the normalisation key.

trigger: every hourly tick with a populated curation queue
classification_rationale: The reconcile UPDATE touched every joined queue row each tick although the docs called the writes changes-only
summary: Fixed: the UPDATE is guarded by IS DISTINCT FROM on device_count and re-stamps last_seen_at at most daily; the ponytail comment names the real bound; background_jobs.hpp and the ADR say selection, not every write, is changes-only.

trigger: a sustained outage where the failing tick period is 3600 s plus the tick duration
classification_rationale: A 2h window holds one increment for about two minutes of every period, so the alert dropped below its threshold and reset its hold once an hour
summary: Fixed: increase over 3h with >= 2; a promtool case at a 61 minute period asserts continuous firing inside each would-be gap; the case turns red when the rule is put back to 2h (evaluations at 182, 243 and 304 minutes).

trigger: an operator following either normalisation alert
classification_rationale: Both annotations named a SoftwareNormalizationJob log that does not exist
summary: Fixed: the annotations name the real log prefixes 'Software normalisation:' and 'SoftwareTitleDimension:'.

trigger: a healthy drain with no REST or UI to observe it
classification_rationale: A healthy tick logged nothing, so progress was invisible
summary: Adapted: one info line per healthy tick (passes, titles, state, next wait); no new counter, so the seven-family list and its docs are unchanged.

trigger: a reader of the data inventory
classification_rationale: The product registry row listed two tables and a populated-only-while-licensing note that v2 made false
summary: Fixed: the existing row now lists the pack, the permanent dimension and the queue, their retention, and that the normalisation job populates them unconditionally. No new framing elsewhere.

trigger: a reader of the seed header, the manual, the ladder or the HA doc
classification_rationale: Published text named plan ids and an unrun measurement, the HA doc counted 48 passes, and several terms were inexact
summary: Fixed: neutral seed header (the seed sha changes, which is fine before release), the manual says a settled title is not re-resolved and how to inspect the tables, the ladder row names the boot refusal and its log prefix, the HA doc counts 49 and names the thread, SET LOCAL then try-lock wording, macos_pkgutil, install-weighted, pack_info label growth, and a follow-up without an issue number.

trigger: title_dimension grows with every distinct title ever seen
classification_rationale: The permanent, unbounded dimension and the queue's no-would-wipe reconcile were decisions nobody had recorded
summary: Fixed: the ledger row, the ADR update and the manual record the accepted bound (distinct triples ever seen), why there is no prune, that a later prune routes through the clock-guarded-retention rule, and that the queue reconcile is a derived-set reconcile with deliberately no would-wipe guard.

trigger: a later change to the normalisation files
classification_rationale: No routed-concern row named the new files, so no reviewer was loaded for them
summary: Fixed (adapted): one row in the software-estate table, which has room; routed-concerns.md (over its budget) is untouched.

trigger: the advisory lock answering with an unexpected shape
classification_rationale: try_norm_lock read zero tuples or any non-'f' value as 'we hold the lock', and run_tick documented 'never throws' without saying why
summary: Fixed: held only on exactly one row of 't', 'f' is a peer, anything else is a failed pass (logged); run_tick's contract says each stage catches and that the cancel predicate must not throw. The unexpected-shape branch cannot be produced from a real Postgres, so it is pinned by inspection and the peer-held and held paths are exercised in the [pg] cases.

trigger: a consumer reading the provisional seed's results
classification_rationale: The seed's Windows-only bindings, version-token behaviour, publisher-unverified generic names and short canonical titles were not documented
summary: Fixed: one 'Known limits of the seed pack' bullet in the manual and a ledger line; no behaviour change.

trigger: a regression in cancellation, upgrade, reconcile or array round-trip behaviour
classification_rationale: Cancellation after the first write, the v1 to v2 upgrade over live rows, the reconcile lock-skip, array metacharacters and named selection of two test cases had no coverage
summary: Fixed: cases for each (see the resource ledger for the mutation evidence), the two comma-bearing names renamed, parser negatives that assert the reason, a candidate ordering case, awkward-name round trips, seed rows resolved end to end in both the pure and the database layers, job lifecycle sections that wait on a completed tick, and the cancelled-tick and capped-cleared metric cases.

trigger: a C++ change without its governance fragment and Resource Ledger
classification_rationale: No governance.d fragment or Resource Ledger row existed for the change
summary: Fixed: this fragment and governance.d/feat-sw-sam-normalization.FV9Phx.resource-ledger.md are committed with the owners, bounds and decision lines.
